newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta starts around Friday's level, tight range seen.
newsitem.headline: Peseta starts around Friday's level, tight range seen.

text.p: The peseta opened unchanged against a generally weak mark on Monday, holding the level it climbed to at the end of last week, dealers said.
"It has little to do with the peseta. It's more a general outlook, due to the mark's weakness," a dealer in Madrid said.
He added the peseta could gain further ground today, with a first target at 84.25 to the mark. "If it should break 84.25 then it will aim directly to 84.10," he added.
At 0710 GMT, the peseta was trading at around 84.31/33 versus 84.30/33 on Friday evening. It had begun Friday at 84.43/45.
"It's mainly a dollar driven thing. If the dollar stays where it is now I do not see any reason why the peseta should gain more," an analyst in Madrid said.
Other dealers added that expectations that the Bank of Spain would hold its official rate unchanged for the summer were supporting the Spanish unit.
The Bank of Spain holds its next official repo tomorrow and experts forecast no change in the key money market rate.
Against the dollar the peseta was weaker, trading at around 149.90/145.00 versus 149.27/33 on Friday evening.
